title: Sandboxed Scheduler: Economic Admission & Canary Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This playbook documents the experimental scheduler sandbox (sched-sandbox) used to validate cost-aware admission policies, economic priority governor behaviors, and safe canary rollouts for kernel changes. It is intended for runtime engineers, oncall, and performance owners running safety-limited experiments against production-like traffic.

Purpose and scope:
- Reduce risk when introducing scheduler/econ changes by running them in an isolated decision plane that mirrors production inputs.
- Capture SLO regressions, cost deltas, and fidelity impact before full rollout.
- Provide a concrete runbook for activation, monitoring, rollback, and postmortem.

High-level architecture overview:
- sched-sandbox (service): an in-cluster decision plane that accepts a copy of dispatch metadata and returns admission/priority decisions for sampled traffic. It does not affect real dispatch; instead it annotates decisions for comparison.
- kernel-admitter (component): produces observed kernel slot allocations and credits. Sandbox mirrors the API and uses the same kernel hints.
- econ-governor (component): configurable economic model (weights for latency vs cost vs fidelity) used by sched-sandbox to synthesize priority.
- profiling-agent: collects trace fragments, kernel timing, and cost estimates for sandboxed requests.

Design principles:
1) Non-invasive: sandbox must never affect live routing or admission. Make-change-by-annotation only.
2) Deterministic inputs: ensure sampled requests have the same input features (sequence length, model variant, tenant tier, token budget).
3) Low-noise sampling: prefer stratified sampling by tenant and route to ensure representation across latency-sensitive and batchy workloads.
4) Telemetry parity: capture the same telemetry tags as production (kernel_id, slot_count, credit_charge, model_variant, origin_region).

Operational SLOs (for sandbox observability):
- Sample coverage: >= 0.5% of all requests per active route OR at least 5 QPS per route for 95% of time.
- Trace fidelity: 99% of sandbox traces must include kernel_id, kernel_latency_ms, and credit_cost_estimate.
- Canary detection latency: sandbox must detect a statistically significant SLO shift within 30 minutes for a sustained regression lasting 5 minutes.

Admission policy and economic model (econ-governor):
The econ-governor computes a numeric priority score P per request: P = w_L * normalized_latency_sensitivity + w_C * normalized_cost_sensitivity + w_F * fidelity_penalty.
- Weights are declared per-experiment and can be tuned in the sandbox UI.
- Normalization uses percentiles from a 7-day rolling window (p50..p99.9) per route.

Configuration table (canonical knobs):
| knob | description | default | safe-range |
|------|-------------|---------|------------|
| sampling_rate | Fraction of requests mirrored to sandbox | 0.005 | 0.001 - 0.02 |
| econ_weights | [w_L,w_C,w_F] vector | [0.6,0.3,0.1] | each 0.0 - 1.0, sum>0 |
| admission_queue_limit | Max concurrent sandboxed admissions queued | 200 | 50 - 1000 |
| drift_alert_threshold | Relative delta from production decision rate to trigger review | 5% | 1% - 20% |
| canary_window_minutes | Sliding window for canary decision aggregation | 30 | 5 - 120 |

Canary and experiment lifecycle (step-by-step):
1) Plan: create experiment entry in the experiments registry with objectives, owner, and primary metrics (cost per token delta, p99 latency, fidelity rollback rate).
2) Baseline capture: run sandbox with current production econ_weights for 24–72 hours to capture baseline decision distribution and kernel hints.
3) Pilot: deploy modified econ_weights or scheduler policy to sched-sandbox only at sampling_rate = 0.5%.
4) Shadow analysis: run automated comparison job that computes the following per-route metrics every 10 minutes:
   a) Decision flip rate (fraction of requests where sandbox decision differs from production).
   b) Delta cost estimate (sandbox_est - production_est) per-token and per-request.
   c) SLO delta (p50,p95,p99) predicted from kernel_latency models.
5) Canary escalation: if metrics within acceptance band for 4 consecutive windows, increase sampling_rate to 2% and repeat.
6) Live canary: with approval, route 1% real traffic to new scheduler policy (controlled canary). If safe, scale to 10% then full rollout.

Acceptance bands (default):
- Cost per-token increase: <= 3%
- p99 latency predicted increase: <= 5% absolute ms or <= 10% relative (whichever larger)
- Decision flip rate: <= 8% for high-volume routes, <= 15% for low-volume routes

Automated analysis and alerts:
- Daily experiment report summarizing cost and SLO deltas (owner: runtime-experiments@redwood.com).
- Immediate alert (pager) if predicted p99 latency increases by > 50ms or decision flip rate > 25% sustained for two windows.
- Drift alert when sandbox decisions diverge from production at > drift_alert_threshold; this triggers an investigation ticket.

Profiling and benchmarking protocol for experiments:
1) Synthetic fidelity replay: replay a slice of production traffic (stored in request-corpus) through the sandbox with and without the change to compute kernel occupancy differences.
2) Microbench patch: run kernel-level microbenchmarks with stress harness to estimate worst-case slot contention and thermal influence.
3) Shadow benchmarks: run the bench-suite (bench-run) with the candidate scheduler policy against a mirrored cluster to measure throughput and tail-latency under mixed workloads.

Example CLI snippets:
- Enable sandbox for experiment EX-123:
  rctl experiments create --id EX-123 --owner aisha --weights 0.5,0.4,0.1 --sampling 0.005
- Increase sampling rate:
  rctl experiments update --id EX-123 --sampling 0.02
- Fetch last 30m comparison summary:
  rctl experiments summary --id EX-123 --window 30m --format table

Runbook: urgent triage (if sandbox flags a regression):
1) Acknowledge alert and page runtime-sre and the experiment owner.
2) Immediately pause the experiment sampling (set sampling_rate=0).
3) Capture a forensic sweep: export sandbox traces, kernel snapshots, and bench-suite results for the last 60 minutes.
4) Rollback any canary routing if in live canary stage.
5) Triage with the kernel team: inspect kernel_id distribution and credit exhaustion signals.
6) If root cause is econ weights, revert to baseline weights and re-run baseline capture for 24 hours.
7) Produce a postmortem within 72 hours if the incident impacted production latency or cost beyond escalation thresholds.

Ownership, roles and contacts:
- Runtime experimentation owner: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.com)
- Kernel instrumentation: Jonah Kim (jonah@redwood.com)
- SRE paging rota: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.com

Safety checklist before promoting a scheduler change to production:
1) Baseline capture completed and reviewed.
2) Shadow and synthetic replay show cost delta within acceptance band.
3) Bench-suite shows no >10% regression in throughput for critical routes.
4) Canary plan documented with rollback windows and owners.
5) Alerts and dashboards created (grafana urls inserted in the experiment page).

Metrics and dashboards to create for each experiment (minimum):
- Decision flip rate by route (1m, 5m quantiles)
- Estimated cost delta per-token (rolling 1h)
- Kernel occupancy heatmap (by kernel_id x slot_count)
- Predicted vs observed p99 latency (compare model estimate and production measurement)

Post-experiment checklist and follow-up:
- If promoted: update runtime-contracts and scheduler-policy registry with new weights and policy id.
- If rejected: archive experiment and note root-cause, suggested mitigations, and next steps.
- Add a short summary to the weekly runtime experiment digest.
